content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Software Developer | Frontend and Web Applications
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
GitHub: github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing graduate with First Class Honours and practical experience building and testing web applications. Developed a React and TypeScript project with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL database, and contributed accessibility fixes and reusable components to a production React news site during an internship. Experienced with Git, automated testing, API integration and documenting components in Storybook.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming: JavaScript, TypeScript
Web and application development: React, Next.js, Node.js, Express, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Data and APIs: PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication, public API integration
Testing and quality: Jest, React Testing Library, accessibility (WCAG 2.1), screen-reader testing
Tools: Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma, Vercel

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing - Software Development, First Class Honours
Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
Final year project: “Tidewatch” — accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers, built with React, TypeScript, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL. Achieved 82% (First Class) and was demonstrated at the college project showcase.
Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms

RELEVANT EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, with statically generated marketing pages, a class timetable and booking requests sent by email.
- Deployed the website on Vercel and enabled content updates through Markdown files.
- Made small updates to two WordPress sites.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Contributed to the company's React news site as part of the web team.
- Fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit across 20+ components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels.
- Built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it with Storybook stories.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app displaying tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Developed the React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.

Transit Delay Notifier | Student Hackathon | 2024
- Worked in a three-person team that placed second in a student hackathon, building a transit delay notifier in 24 hours.
- Developed the frontend.

Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a four-person student project: a web app for matching classmates for study sessions.
- Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of web development labs.

Barista (part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025

COMMUNITY
- Run social media for a sea swimming club.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional and substantially stronger than the original CV. It presents a clear summary, logically grouped technical skills, quantified internship impact (20+ components), relevant projects, testing experience and accessibility work. The Tidewatch project is particularly effective because it demonstrates full-stack development, API integration, testing and a measurable accessibility result. Education, project dates and employment history are clear. The main content limitation is not writing quality but role relevance: the CV is strongly frontend/web-focused and contains little evidence of infrastructure, operations, systems or networking work required for an SRE programme. The summary also says "Experienced with" several areas when the evidence is primarily academic, project-based or internship-based; using more precise wording would improve credibility.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly headings, conventional chronology, plain text formatting and clearly separated skills, education, experience and projects. Relevant terms such as Git, testing, APIs, deployment, Node.js, PostgreSQL, accessibility and documentation are easy to parse. However, AI/ATS screening probability for this specific SRE role is low to moderate because the document does not contain the required programming languages (Python, Go, C++ or Java), networking terms such as Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP or routing, or containers, Kubernetes and GitOps. These are candidate gaps rather than keywords that can be safely added. The document also gives greater prominence to frontend technologies than to deployment, operational responsibility or systems-related learning. Do not add unsupported infrastructure keywords merely to improve matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows a recent First Class Computing graduate, Git familiarity, testing, documentation, API work, deployment on Vercel and experience contributing to a production web site. These support the programme's expectations around writing tests, documenting work, completing defined projects and learning in an engineering team. The hackathon, teaching-assistant work and internship also provide some evidence of collaboration, initiative and communication. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate the role's core requirements for right to work in Finland, programming in Python/Go/C++/Java, networking fundamentals, cloud-platform and operations knowledge, hardware/software fundamentals, containers, Kubernetes or GitOps. The CV therefore represents a credible junior web developer but not a current strong match for this SRE programme. The document does not establish Finnish work authorization; the original notes only state authorization to work in Ireland under a Stamp 1G visa.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, replace "Experienced with Git, automated testing, API integration and documenting components in Storybook" with more precise wording such as "Hands-on experience with Git, automated testing, API integration, Vercel deployment and documenting reusable components in Storybook through academic, freelance and internship projects." This avoids overstating professional SRE experience while preserving truthful transferable evidence.

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, change the category label "Web and application development" to "Web application development" and keep the existing tools there. Do not add cloud, infrastructure, Linux, container, Kubernetes, GitOps or networking keywords because they are not supported by the candidate information.

MINOR — In the Tidewatch project entry, make the operationally relevant evidence more explicit by changing the second bullet to: "Developed the React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that cached data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites." Retain the existing testing and accessibility bullet. This makes the API, data and application-behaviour evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without presenting it as infrastructure experience.

MINOR — In the Frontend Developer experience entry, change "Deployed the website on Vercel" to "Deployed the website on Vercel and maintained content updates through Markdown files." This more clearly shows deployment and ongoing maintenance while remaining within the documented experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "production React news site"

requirements.requirement: Genuine interest in, and basic knowledge of, cloud platforms, operations, networking, hardware and software
Programming experience in at least one of Python, Go, C++ or Java
Understanding of networking basics (Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP, routing)
Basic understanding of containers, Kubernetes and GitOps

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a well-structured, readable and professional CV for a junior frontend or junior full-stack developer. It presents education, experience and projects clearly, uses measurable details such as “20+ components,” “approximately 30 students,” and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100, and explains the candidate’s actual technical contributions. The summary is concise and the document demonstrates credible practical experience rather than relying only on coursework. The main content limitation is role focus: most evidence concerns frontend development, accessibility and web testing, while the target role is Site Reliability Engineering. The CV does not demonstrate core SRE areas such as Linux operations, networking, containers, Kubernetes, GitOps or infrastructure automation. These are candidate-to-role gaps, not writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard date ranges, bullet points and clearly grouped skills. It contains strong searchable terms for web development, including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Git, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook and WCAG 2.1. AI/ATS screening is therefore likely to identify a strong junior frontend profile, but the match probability for this particular SRE vacancy is substantially lower because the document contains none of the required programming languages listed in the advert (Python, Go, C++ or Java), and does not contain networking, containers, Kubernetes or GitOps terminology. “Vercel” supports limited cloud/deployment relevance, but does not establish cloud infrastructure or operations experience. The use of standard headings is good; adding full https:// prefixes to the GitHub and portfolio URLs would make those links more reliably clickable and parseable.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a recent Computing graduate with relevant software development experience, testing experience and Git familiarity. The CV shows some adjacent evidence for the role: Vercel deployment, API integration, automated tests, documentation in Storybook, and practical software development. However, the target role’s core requirements are not met by the supplied candidate information. The candidate material does not show right to work in Finland; it states the candidate can work full time in Ireland under a Stamp 1G visa. It also does not show programming experience in Python, Go, C++ or Java, networking fundamentals such as Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP or routing, or basic understanding of containers, Kubernetes and GitOps. Cloud-platform exposure is limited to Vercel, and there is no evidence of operations, hardware, Linux systems, infrastructure automation, ticket backlogs, issue tracking or production service ownership. The strongest truthful positioning is as an early-career software developer with adjacent deployment, testing and API experience, rather than as an already-qualified SRE candidate.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / role-targeting improvements:
1. In the Professional Summary section, keep the existing frontend evidence but make the transferable engineering practices more prominent. For example, replace the final sentence with: “Hands-on experience with Git, automated testing, API integration, deployment on Vercel, accessibility testing and documenting reusable components in Storybook across academic, freelance and internship projects.” This is more concise and surfaces terms relevant to the advert without claiming unsupported SRE experience.
2. In the Technical Skills section, retain the current skills but make deployment and engineering practices easier to identify by changing “Tools: Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma, Vercel” to “Version control and deployment: Git, GitHub, Vercel; Documentation and design: Storybook, Figma.” Do not add Linux, containers, Kubernetes, GitOps, Terraform, Helm, networking or Python/Go/C++/Java because they are not supported by the candidate information.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change “public API integration” to “Public API integration” and ensure all skill labels use consistent capitalization. This improves keyword parsing and visual consistency.
4. In the contact line, change “github.com/aiyana-bt-example” and “aiyana-bt.example.com” to “https://github.com/aiyana-bt-example” and “https://aiyana-bt.example.com” so ATS and recruiter software can recognize them as complete URLs.
5. In the Projects section under Tidewatch, retain the existing API, testing and accessibility details but explicitly preserve the supported deployment/testing terminology already used elsewhere. For example, the technology line can read: “Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js and Jest; tested with NVDA and VoiceOver.” This gives screening systems a compact, evidence-based view of software quality practices.

MINOR enhancement:
6. In the Experience section under “Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance),” change “Deployed the website on Vercel” to “Deployed the website on Vercel and maintained content updates through Markdown files.” This combines the deployment and maintenance evidence into one stronger, still truthful bullet.
